---
title: "llms.txt: a markdown mirror for AI tools"
---

## Overview

Language-model tools read markdown far better than they read rendered
HTML. With one line of configuration, Quarto publishes a
machine-friendly mirror of your website alongside the normal HTML
output:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
website:
  llms-txt: true
```

Rendering the site then produces, in the output directory:

- **A markdown companion for every page.** `about.html` gets an
  `about.md` sibling — a clean markdown rendering of the page's
  content, with navigation, scripts, and styling chrome left out.
- **`llms.txt`** — an organized index of those companions, following
  the [llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org): the site title, a
  short description, and sections of annotated links.
- **`llms-full.txt`** — every companion concatenated into a single
  file, for tools that prefer one big context document.

The feature only applies to **website** projects. In any other
project type Quarto warns that the key has no effect rather than
ignoring it.

## What the index looks like

`llms.txt` mirrors your site's navigation. Each sidebar section
becomes a heading, and each page becomes a link annotated with the
page's `description:` from its front matter:

```markdown
# Acme Documentation

> Reference and guides for the Acme toolkit.

## Getting started

- [Installation](install.md): Installing Acme on every platform
- [First steps](first-steps.md): Your first Acme project

## Reference

- [CLI reference](cli.md): Every command and flag
```

The organization rules:

- **Sidebar sections** become `##` headings, in the order you
  declared them. A site with several sidebars gets one heading per
  sidebar instead.
- Pages the sidebar doesn't reach are appended under a final
  `## Other` heading, so every page is always indexed.
- The **home page** is pinned to the top when no sidebar section
  covers it.
- A site with no sidebar at all lists everything under one
  `## Pages` heading.
- When `website.site-url` is set, links are absolute URLs; otherwise
  they're relative.

Give your pages one-line `description:` entries in their front
matter — they become the annotations that make the index genuinely
useful to an AI assistant deciding which page to read.

## Links between companions

Inside a companion, links to other pages of your site point at the
*markdown* siblings, not the HTML — a tool that starts at `llms.txt`
stays inside the markdown mirror as it follows links. Links to
drafts, external sites, and non-page files are left untouched.

## Choosing a link's target: `link-format`

Sometimes the automatic choice is not the one you want. The
`link-format` link attribute picks which output of the target page a
link points at:

```markdown
[View this page as Markdown](index.qmd){link-format="llms"}

[Try the interactive demo](demo.qmd){link-format="html"}
```

- **`link-format="llms"`** points the link at the target page's
  markdown companion — even on the HTML page. Use it for a "view as
  markdown" affordance, or to hand AI-oriented reading paths to your
  readers. Linking a page's *own* source path, as above, links its
  own companion.
- **`link-format="html"`** keeps the link on the HTML page, even
  inside markdown companions (which normally rewrite same-site links
  to `.md` siblings). Use it when the target's value is its rendered
  presentation — an interactive demo, a figure gallery — and the
  markdown mirror would miss the point.

Write the target as the page's **source path** (`guide/index.qmd`),
exactly as you would for any other internal link; the attribute alone
selects the output. A request that cannot be honored — an unknown
value, a target that isn't a project page, a `llms` pin without
`llms-txt: true` or on a draft — leaves the link resolving normally
and warns with
[`Q-13-9`](../../errors/navigation/Q-13-9.qmd).

## Showing content only to AI tools (or only to people)

The markdown mirror is a conditional-content target named `llms`.
Use it with the standard `.content-visible` / `.content-hidden`
conditional-content divs (also used for
[project profiles](profiles.qmd)):

```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-format="llms"}
Note for AI assistants: the full API schema is at [api.md](api.md).
:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="llms"}
This interactive demo requires a browser.
:::
```

The first block appears only in the markdown companion; the second
only on the HTML page. Everything else appears in both — the
companion mirrors the HTML view, so content conditioned
`when-format="html"` stays in it.

Prefer prose inside these blocks: a heading inside an
`llms`-only block can still surface in the page's table of contents,
and cross-referenceable figures inside one are not numbered.

## Drafts and the 404 page

Pages marked `draft: true` and the site's `404.qmd` still render to
HTML as usual, but get no markdown companion and never appear in
`llms.txt` or `llms-full.txt`.

## Quarto never overwrites your files

Companion paths share a namespace with your own files: a copied
resource named `about.md` occupies the exact path where the
companion of `about.html` wants to live. Quarto keeps a record of the files *it*
generated (in `.quarto/llms-manifest.json`) and refuses to overwrite
anything else — the render fails with
[`Q-5-28`](../../errors/project/Q-5-28.qmd) naming the contested
path, and you choose: rename the file, drop it from
`project.resources`, or turn `llms-txt` off.
